prompts.text: Which part of preparing food together feels relaxing to you, and which part feels like work?
Pick a recipe together before shopping or choose ingredients at the market and decide later?
Tell me about a meal from your family home which has a particular memory attached to it.
We accidentally buy ingredients for two different dinners. What would you make from both?
Cooking styles often reveal whether someone likes precise instructions or a little improvisation.
Sharing responsibility for meals matters more than taking turns with the exact same chores.
What kitchen task would you happily teach me if I wanted to learn?
Recall a time a dish went wrong and we enjoyed the evening anyway.
One of us wants to host dinner and the other worries about the work involved. What would make hosting fair?
A simple dish we prepare well or a new recipe neither of us has tried?
How do you like to spend the first ten minutes after you get home?
Coming home feels different when someone understands whether you need conversation or quiet.
Describe a day when something ordinary at home helped you recover from a tiring experience.
Our weekend plans fall through at the last minute. What's your favourite way to rescue the day?
Small rituals are worth protecting even when nobody else understands their importance.
Which corner of our home would you like to make more comfortable?
Spend an afternoon rearranging furniture or browse second-hand shops for a useful find?
Tell me about a room you once lived in which felt completely yours.
We inherit a piece of furniture with sentimental value, but it doesn't suit our space. How should we decide?
People sometimes disagree about clutter because objects carry different memories for them.
What do you think makes visitors feel welcome without requiring a perfect house?
Keeping a home pleasant is a shared responsibility, not a measure of one person's care.
A neighbour regularly asks us for favours. How should we decide what we're comfortable offering?
Recall an occasion when someone welcomed us into their home in a way you appreciated.
Invite two close friends for an unhurried evening or gather a larger group for games?
Which friendships would you like us to make more time to nurture?
Some friends become part of a couple's shared life while others remain important individually.
Tell me about a friend who influenced the way you approach relationships.
A friend confides in one of us about a sensitive matter. How do we respect their privacy as a couple?
Trust includes knowing which stories belong to someone else.
What helps you feel confident speaking up when you disagree with a plan I suggest?
Talk through a decision immediately or each think it over and return to it later?
Describe a time you changed your mind during a conversation without feeling pressured.
I interrupt you while you're explaining something important. How would you like me to correct it?
Some people think aloud while others need time before they know what they mean.
Which expression or tone tends to make a conversation feel more tense than intended?
Listening well sometimes means asking one clear question instead of offering a quick solution.
Remember a question I asked which showed I had been paying attention.
A discussion gets heated before guests arrive. How should we handle it without pretending nothing happened?
Leave a disagreement unresolved until morning or pause it and agree on a time to revisit?
What makes you feel appreciated on days when you haven't achieved anything notable?
Tell me about receiving encouragement which felt specific rather than routine.
Praise means more to some people when it names the effort behind the result.
You've spent hours on a project which doesn't work out. What kind of evening would help you reset?
Support should leave people room to make their own decisions.
When have you felt proud of something you did quietly without telling many people?
Mark the end of a demanding week with a favourite meal or with an early night?
Describe a small success you almost overlooked until someone pointed it out.
We each complete a difficult task on the same day. How would you like us to celebrate together?
A person might need reassurance after a success as much as after a setback.
What is one skill you admire in me which you think I underestimate?
Being curious about your partner's work matters even when the field is unfamiliar.
Tell me about the first time you explained a passion of yours and felt I understood the appeal.
I ask you for feedback on something personal. How should I make clear whether I want candour or encouragement?
Read side by side in silence or share an article and discuss it afterwards?
Which subject would you enjoy studying for no reason beyond interest?
People sometimes reveal new sides of themselves when they become beginners again.
Describe a hobby you left behind and what made it important at the time.
We sign up to learn something together and both find it harder than expected. What would keep us motivated?
Trying a new activity together works best when neither person feels pressured to excel.
Which belief or principle guides your decisions when the easy option feels wrong?
Tell me about someone who taught you what fairness in a partnership looks like.
Talk about values during a long drive or write down thoughts separately and compare them?
A choice benefits us but inconveniences someone we care about. How should we weigh their needs?
People sometimes share a value while disagreeing about how to practise it.
What personal conviction would you want me to respect even if I don't share it?
Respecting a difference is more meaningful than claiming the difference never matters.
Recall a conversation where you learnt why someone saw a moral question differently.
A family gathering includes a conversation we both find uncomfortable. How would you like us to support each other?
Leave a gathering together at an agreed time or decide when we're ready on the day?
Which signs tell you you're starting to feel overwhelmed before you say anything?
One partner might process worry by talking while the other prefers to do something practical.
Describe a time you took a rest you initially thought you hadn't earned.
We're both managing difficult personal news. What does giving each other space without withdrawing look like?
Checking how someone wants to receive support beats assuming you already know.
What would a genuinely restful day look like if there were no expectations from anyone?
A day without screens or a day without commitments?
Tell me about the last time you felt fully rested and what helped.
One of us needs a medical appointment and feels nervous. What kind of company or help would be welcome?
Looking after your health gets easier when practical support doesn't take away your independence.
How do you feel about keeping shared calendars for our plans while maintaining personal privacy?
Convenience doesn't require sharing every password or private conversation.
One of us wants to post a photograph while the other prefers to keep the moment private. What should decide?
Put phones away during meals or agree on a screen-free hour each evening?
Recall a time a photograph or recording changed the way you remembered an occasion.
Which online habit would you most like us to improve together?
People develop different expectations about how quickly a message deserves a reply.
I'm busy and see your message but don't have time for a proper answer. Which response would you appreciate?
A delayed reply doesn't automatically mean someone's attention has changed.
Which shared memory would you choose to revisit if we had only one photograph from it?
Tell me about a surprising detail you noticed on a day we spent together.
Make an album of our favourite moments or keep a small box of tickets and notes?
We're choosing which old belongings to keep before moving. What would deserve space because of its story?
Sentimental objects often mean more after somebody explains the memory connected to them.
What part of our story would you want us to tell with greater care when we look back?
A good relationship leaves room for ordinary days that never become special occasions.
Describe a lesson about patience you've learnt from living or planning life alongside me.
Tomorrow offers us both a fresh start after an awkward week. What small change would you want us to make first?
End the day sharing one good moment or begin the morning naming one thing we're looking forward to?
What would you like us to remember about how we treated each other this year?
